d1r-tracks-da-50ms-delay: D1 receptor occupancy trails extracellular dopamine by about 50 milliseconds and rises only during bursts, not tonic firing.
d2r-initialization-unjustified: Every simulation starts D2 occupancy at a value the model's own parameters do not predict, with no test of how much it matters.
d2r-insensitive-to-brief-pauses: A full one-second pause in firing barely lowers D2 receptor occupancy, across a tenfold range of assumed D2 affinity.
d2r-integrates-over-seconds: D2 receptor occupancy takes seconds to fall back after a burst, so it cannot separate closely spaced bursts.
d2r-occupancy-higher-in-vs: During pacemaker firing, D2 receptor occupancy is higher in ventral than dorsal striatum, matching the higher tonic dopamine.
dat-clustering-greater-in-vs: Super-resolution imaging shows the dopamine transporter is more nanoclustered in ventral than in dorsal striatum.
dat-immunostaining-dorsoventral-gradient: Dopamine transporter protein is more abundant in dorsal than ventral striatum, matching the uptake-rate ratio the model assumes.
dat-nanoclustering-slows-clearance: Dense transporter nanoclusters clear dopamine about twice as slowly as evenly spread ones, because dopamine runs out around them.
ds-lacks-pervasive-tonic-da: During pacemaker firing, dorsal striatum holds separate dopamine hotspots with much of the volume empty, not a tonic baseline.
ds-vs-vmax-ratio-assumed: The three-to-one dorsal-to-ventral ratio of transporter uptake capacity is taken from prior literature, not measured here.
fscv-matches-may-wightman-1989: Simulated voltammetry reproduces published recordings where ventral striatum peaks higher than dorsal at every frequency.
hypothesis-d1-d2-temporal-distinction: D1 receptors detect brief dopamine bursts while D2 receptors integrate dopamine over seconds, because their kinetics differ.
hypothesis-nanoclustering-regulates-vmax: Packing transporters into dense nanoclusters lowers their effective uptake capacity even with total transporter unchanged.
hypothesis-vmax-explains-regional-differ: Dorsal hotspots versus ventral tonic coverage follow from the difference in uptake capacity, not from how dopamine is released.
interprets-cragg-rice-vmax-ratio: Earlier voltammetry work established that dopamine uptake capacity is roughly three times higher in dorsal than ventral striatum.
interprets-may-wightman-1989-fscv: May and Wightman found in rat slices that ventral striatum reaches higher evoked dopamine peaks than dorsal at every frequency.
low-burst-no-spillover-high-burst-does: Short low-frequency bursts keep dopamine inside the burst zone, while stronger bursts spill it into a far larger volume.
nanoclustering-constant-vmax-constraint: The nanoclustering simulations hold total uptake capacity fixed, so slower clearance would not follow if clustering added DAT.
nanoclustering-model-varicosity-scale: The nanoclustering work uses a separate tiny-scale model never coupled back to the tissue-scale model of the other figures.
vmat2-gradient-absent: VMAT2, which loads dopamine into vesicles, shows no dorsoventral gradient, so release capacity cannot explain the difference.
vmax-modulation-larger-impact-in-vs: Ventral striatum, running closer to transporter saturation, shifts its tonic dopamine far more than dorsal when uptake changes.
vmax-only-parameter-driving-regional-dif: Of all the parameters swept, only uptake capacity affects dorsal and ventral striatum differently, the rest moving both alike.
vs-low-active-fraction-resembles-ds-dist: Ventral striatum with a twentieth of its terminals active spreads dopamine as widely as dorsal striatum with all of them active.
vs-lowest-percentiles-above-10nm: Even the lowest-concentration parts of ventral striatum stay above ten nanomolar dopamine during pacemaker firing.
vs-maintains-pervasive-tonic-da: With its lower uptake capacity, ventral striatum fills the whole simulated volume with diffuse tonic dopamine, not hotspots.
